findings.title: Missing assertBillingAccess permission check on print route
findings.explanation: The other invoice routes (list and get-by-id) call assertBillingAccess(req.user) before querying. The new /print route skips it. Any authenticated member of the org, including users without billing permission, can read invoice amounts and status. Add assertBillingAccess(req.user) as the first line of the handler. The route is scoped by org, but that doesn't replace the role check.

findings.title: Status and currency are interpolated into HTML without escaping
findings.explanation: invoice.status and invoice.currency are written into the HTML raw, while org_name is escaped. They are probably constrained values today, but nothing in this handler guarantees that. A future free-form status or currency value would become stored XSS. Pass every interpolated value through escapeHtml, or use a template engine that escapes by default.

findings.title: Amount formatting assumes 2-decimal currencies and ignores precision
findings.explanation: Dividing by 100 and calling toFixed(2) is wrong for zero-decimal currencies (JPY) and three-decimal currencies (KWD). For an accounting document this is a correctness risk. Number() on a bigint or numeric column can also lose precision. Use Intl.NumberFormat with the currency's minor-unit exponent, or reuse any existing money formatter. Also check how the serializer represents amount so the two outputs agree.

findings.title: Period dates are rendered in UTC from TIMESTAMPTZ values
findings.explanation: period_start and period_end are TIMESTAMPTZ. Slicing toISOString() shows the UTC date, which can differ by a day from the billing period the customer expects. Period end may also be exclusive, so the printed range could look off by one. Decide on an explicit timezone and inclusive or exclusive semantics for the display.

findings.title: Invoice id is not validated
findings.explanation: Number(req.params.invoiceId) gives NaN for non-numeric input, and for fractional or huge values. Postgres then throws a cast error, which returns a 500 instead of a 404 or 400. The route also doesn't use zod like the list route does. Validate with z.coerce.number().int().positive(). Also confirm that async errors reach the error handler, since Express 4 doesn't catch rejected promises.

findings.title: Response is a bare HTML fragment with no head, charset, or print styling, and no caching headers
findings.explanation: The output has no <html>, <head>, <meta charset>, or <title>, so it renders in quirks mode and non-ASCII org names may display wrongly. There is no print CSS. Invoice data is sensitive, so add Cache-Control: private, no-store. Consider a Content-Security-Policy header too. If the feature is meant to be a download, add Content-Disposition. The PR title says download but the endpoint just renders inline.

findings.title: No tests for the new endpoint
findings.explanation: The PR adds no tests. Cover at least these cases: success, cross-org access returning 404, a caller without billing access, a non-numeric id, and HTML escaping of the org name.

findings.title: Inline escapeHtml helper and duplicated query
findings.explanation: The generic escapeHtml helper is defined at the bottom of a route file. Move it to a shared util or use a templating library. The invoice query also repeats the logic of the get-by-id route. Consider a shared data-access function.
